# Svifa: smooth scroll for the web (@arcwrightstudio/svifa)

> A smooth scroll library for the browser: the mouse wheel and the trackpad scroll smoothly, on the whole page or inside any
> scrolling element. Plain JavaScript with no dependencies; works with any framework or none. The keyboard, the scroll bar, touch
> and find in page stay the browser's own. Svifa moves the real scroll position, so sticky elements, IntersectionObserver and
> scroll events keep working. The end of a glide is drawn between pixels on the GPU (Chrome, Edge, WebKit), with no CSS: Svifa
> gives the blocks that scroll a layer of their own. Drawn on whole pixels (in Firefox, or with subpixel: false) a glide never moves
> slower than 60 px a second, so its end never stands still and hops. Scrolling boxes inside glide too. The same timing at any
> refresh rate.

This file is the complete reference for writing code that uses Svifa. The README has the same with more explanation.

## Install

npm install @arcwrightstudio/svifa (or pnpm add, yarn add, bun add, deno add npm:@arcwrightstudio/svifa)

Script tag: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@arcwrightstudio/svifa@1.2.0/dist/svifa.global.min.js sets window.Svifa.

## Rules that matter

- Create Svifa only in the browser: in an effect, onMounted, onMount, afterNextRender, a client-only plugin, or a script tag.
  Importing the package on the server is safe (Node 14 or later); `new Svifa()` on the server throws.
- One Svifa per scroller. Creating a second for the same scroller throws until the first is destroyed. Create it once, near the
  root, and call destroy() when whatever created it goes away.
- To scroll from code, call svifa.scrollTo(...), not window.scrollTo: a scroll Svifa did not make ends any glide at once.
- Optional CSS: import '@arcwrightstudio/svifa/svifa.css' (stop() then also holds the keyboard and the scroll bar).
- Reduced motion is followed by default: the wheel stays the browser's and scrollTo moves at once.
- A scroller with scroll-snap-type is left to the browser (the wheel scrolls natively; scrollTo moves at once) unless the snap
  option is on: then Svifa glides to its snap points and rests exactly where the browser would (see Options).
- Works under a strict Content Security Policy, Trusted Types included: no inline script or style, no eval, nothing fetched.

## Plain JavaScript

```js
import Svifa from '@arcwrightstudio/svifa'
import '@arcwrightstudio/svifa/svifa.css'

const svifa = new Svifa({ lerp: 0.1 })
svifa.scrollTo('#pricing', { offset: -80 })
const stop = svifa.on('scroll', ({ scroll, progress, velocity, direction }) => {})
svifa.destroy()
```

## React and Next.js (@arcwrightstudio/svifa/react, needs react 18 or 19)

```tsx
import { SmoothScroll, useSvifa } from '@arcwrightstudio/svifa/react'
import '@arcwrightstudio/svifa/svifa.css'

// app/layout.tsx (a server layout can render it: it is a client component)
<body><SmoothScroll lerp={0.08}>{children}</SmoothScroll></body>

// any component inside (in Next.js a client component, 'use client')
const svifa = useSvifa()                              // Svifa | null (null on the server and until made)
useSvifa((g) => setProgress(g.progress))             // called on every scroll
<button onClick={() => svifa?.scrollTo('top')}>Top</button>
```

SmoothScroll props are the options below; `scroller` may also be a ref. Changing lerp, duration, easing, wheel, wheelSpeed, nested,
native, chain, anchors or snap retunes the running Svifa (a prop taken off goes back to its default); changing scroller, axis,
subpixel (true, false or a selector), reducedMotion or autoRaf makes it again. Works under StrictMode.

## Vue and Nuxt (@arcwrightstudio/svifa/vue, needs vue 3.3 or later)

```vue
<script setup>
import { SmoothScroll, useSvifa } from '@arcwrightstudio/svifa/vue'
import '@arcwrightstudio/svifa/svifa.css'          // Nuxt: css: ['@arcwrightstudio/svifa/svifa.css'] in nuxt.config.ts
</script>
<template><SmoothScroll :lerp="0.08"><RouterView /></SmoothScroll></template>   <!-- Nuxt: <NuxtPage /> in app/app.vue -->
```

Inside it: `const svifa = useSvifa()` (a ref, null on the server and until made), `useSvifa((g) => (progress.value = g.progress))`.
Props as React's; `scroller` may also be a template ref (null waits for it). A flag written alone is on (`<SmoothScroll anchors>`);
one left out keeps its default. It renders only what it holds.

## Svelte and SvelteKit (@arcwrightstudio/svifa/svelte, needs svelte 4 or 5)

```svelte
<script>
  // src/routes/+layout.svelte for a whole SvelteKit site
  import { smoothScroll, useSvifa } from '@arcwrightstudio/svifa/svelte'
  import '@arcwrightstudio/svifa/svifa.css'
  const svifa = smoothScroll({ lerp: 0.08 })      // a store: $svifa is null on the server and until made
</script>
```

Call smoothScroll while the component starts; it makes the Svifa on mount and takes it off on destroy, and shares the store with
components inside: `useSvifa()` returns it, `useSvifa((g) => (progress = g.progress))` also listens. For an element: `smoothScroll({
scroller: () => box })` with `bind:this={box}`. Retune with `$svifa?.configure({ lerp })`.

## Solid (@arcwrightstudio/svifa/solid, needs solid-js 1.6 or later)

```tsx
import { SmoothScroll, useSvifa } from '@arcwrightstudio/svifa/solid'
<SmoothScroll lerp={0.08}>{props.children}</SmoothScroll>
const svifa = useSvifa()                               // an accessor: svifa() is null on the server and until made
useSvifa((g) => setProgress(g.progress))
```

Props as React's; `scroller` may also be a function returning an element (one set with ref).

## Angular (@arcwrightstudio/svifa/angular, needs @angular/core 19 or later)

```ts
// app.config.ts
providers: [provideSmoothScroll({ lerp: 0.08 })]
// any component or service (injection context): a signal, null until made
svifa = injectSvifa()
constructor() { injectSvifa((g) => this.progress.set(g.progress)) }
// a Svifa of a component's own, for a scrolling element from a view query
box = viewChild.required<ElementRef<HTMLElement>>('box')
boxed = createSvifa(() => ({ scroller: this.box().nativeElement }))
```

Made after the first render, only in the browser, outside Angular's zone; works with zone.js and without. Add
node_modules/@arcwrightstudio/svifa/svifa.css to styles in angular.json.

## Astro (@arcwrightstudio/svifa/astro)

```astro
---
import SmoothScroll from '@arcwrightstudio/svifa/astro'
---
<SmoothScroll lerp={0.08} anchors={{ offset: -80 }} />   <!-- once, in a layout; it brings the stylesheet -->
```

Props are the options that can be written in markup (not easing or native); scroller is a CSS selector, subpixel true, false or
a selector, nested true, false or 'native'. With view
transitions (<ClientRouter />) a Svifa is made for each page. A script reaches it as document.querySelector('svifa-scroll').svifa.

## Without a component

Make it in the browser and destroy it when whatever made it goes away: `const svifa = new Svifa()` in an effect, onMounted,
onMount, afterNextRender or a script tag, then `svifa.destroy()`.

## Options (new Svifa(options))

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| scroller | window | The page, or a scrolling element (overflow auto or scroll). |
| axis | 'vertical' | 'horizontal' for a sideways scroller (right-to-left content included); it takes the wheel's up and down too. 'both' glides up and down and sideways at once (each axis its own part of the wheel; Shift with a mouse wheel moves it sideways). |
| lerp | 0.1 | Smoothness, the same at any refresh rate: about this share of the remaining distance every 1/60 s (on whole pixels never slower than 60 px/s). 0.16 snappy, 0.07 soft, 0.05 slow, 0.03 very slow. At most 1. |
| duration | none | Glide for a set time in seconds instead, along easing; on whole pixels never slower than 60 px/s, so a slow-ending easing arrives a little early there. |
| easing | ease-out | (t: 0..1) => 0..1, for a timed glide. |
| wheel | true | false leaves the wheel to the browser; scrollTo still glides. |
| wheelSpeed | 1 | Multiplies every wheel and trackpad movement. |
| nested | true | A scrolling box inside glides the wheel itself while it can move that way (same feel, drawn between pixels), then hands it on. 'native' leaves boxes to the browser, false glides the scroller over them, (box) => true / false / 'native' / options decides per box. |
| native | none | (element) => boolean: elements whose wheel turns are left to the browser. data-svifa-native on an element does the same. |
| chain | true | For an element scroller: at its start or end the wheel goes on to the page. |
| subpixel | true | Draw between whole pixels while gliding, on blocks Svifa chooses; or a selector, a list or a function naming them; false for whole pixels (see below). |
| anchors | false | true, or scrollTo options: glide to same-page links (#id, #, #top). Adds a history entry, sends hashchange, moves keyboard focus for a link pressed from the keyboard. |
| snap | false | Glide to the snap points the page sets in CSS (scroll-snap-type, scroll-snap-align). The wheel goes as far as it would and rests on the nearest point; mandatory: one notch or swipe moves one point; proximity: rests on a point only within a third of the visible area. scrollTo and same-page links rest on the nearest point. scroll-padding, scroll-margin, scroll-snap-stop and areas longer than the visible area are honoured; every rest is where the browser itself would rest. |
| reducedMotion | true | Follow prefers-reduced-motion. |
| autoRaf | true | false to call svifa.raf(time) from your own loop (GSAP: gsap.ticker.add((t) => svifa.raf(t * 1000))). |

A number that is not finite is taken as its default.

## Methods

- scrollTo(target, options?) => Promise<boolean>. target: a number, an element, a CSS selector or '#id', 'top' | 'start' |
  'bottom' | 'end'; with axis 'both', also { x, y } (a number is then the vertical position; an element, selector or keyword sets
  both). Options: offset (a number, or { x, y } both ways), immediate, lerp, duration, easing, lock (hold the wheel until it
  arrives), force (glide while stopped). An element lands as for a link to it (scroll-margin and scroll-padding honoured; a nested scrolling box is brought into
  view first). Resolves true on arrival, false if something else moved the scroller, the wheel or a later scrollTo took over, Svifa
  is stopped, or the target is missing (with a warning). Never rejects.
- configure(changes): change lerp, duration, easing, wheel, wheelSpeed, nested, native, chain, anchors, snap while running
  (duration: undefined goes back to lerp). Other options are fixed at creation.
- stop() / start(): hold the scroller for a dialog; with svifa.css the keyboard and the scroll bar are held too, and the scroll
  bar's room is kept so nothing shifts.
- on('scroll', listener) returns an unsubscribe function; off('scroll', listener). The listener gets the Svifa instance.
- raf(time): only with autoRaf: false.
- destroy(): removes every listener, class and style; calling it twice is safe.

## Properties

scroll (current position: exact while gliding, the browser's at rest), target, limit (measured now), progress (0..1), velocity
(px/s), direction (1, -1, 0), isGliding, isStopped, element (<html> for the page), axis, options (read only); x and y, each axis on
its own ({ scroll, target, limit, progress, velocity, direction }, null for an axis it does not move); both ways, the single-axis
properties are the vertical axis. Exports: Svifa (default and named), easeOut, version; types SvifaOptions, ScrollToOptions,
TunableOptions, SvifaTarget, Point, AxisState, Easing, Axis, SvifaEvent, ResolvedOptions. Entries: /react, /vue, /svelte, /solid,
/angular, /astro, /svifa.css.

## Events and classes

The browser's scroll events fire as usual. One scrollend per glide that moved the scroller (detail.svifa === true), on document for
the page. Classes on the scroller's element: svifa, svifa-gliding, svifa-stopped, svifa-subpixel. data-svifa-native on an element
leaves its wheel to the browser; data-svifa-subpixel="off" leaves it on whole pixels (on html or body, the whole page).

## Drawing between pixels (subpixel)

On by default with no CSS. Svifa sets will-change: translate on the scroller's top-level blocks (and sticky elements inside them)
for as long as it runs, splits around a block holding a fixed element or a z-index that reaches past it (a menu), and draws on
whole pixels, with one console warning, where a fixed or sticky element with no z-index is followed by content (fix: give it a
z-index). Each layer is a stacking context; in Chrome and Edge on Windows its text uses greyscale antialiasing. Not in Firefox, on
touch-only devices, while reduced motion is on, or where the browser lacks the translate property. To name the blocks instead:

```js
new Svifa({ subpixel: 'main > section, footer' })
```

Name blocks that together cover what scrolls, and every sticky element inside them. Never a position: fixed element or an ancestor
of one.

## Yarn Plug'n'Play

Every entry works through a bundler, and installing Svifa does not turn on Yarn's experimental ES module loader. Code Node runs
directly under Plug'n'Play loads Svifa with require; an ES module run that way needs that loader (pnpEnableEsmLoader: true).
